rulings.docket_item: P01-007 (surfaced by the phase-1 author correctly REFUSING a disguised boundary change carried inside a peer remedy - the Eccl B-5 pattern): the c01 peer remedy proposed extending the dialogue exchange Song.1.15-Song.2.3 to close at the MT 2:6|2:7 refrain bracket, or re-cutting so the single-voice run beginning inside MT 2:3 is not severed. The author executed only the authorized fallback.
rulings.decision: DECLINE the boundary proposal in both its variants. P01-007 STANDS at Song.1.15-Song.2.3; it does NOT extend to Song.2.6 or Song.2.7, and it is not re-cut. The author's refusal to execute the embedded boundary change was CORRECT and is ratified: a boundary proposal carried inside a remedy is not author-wave work, and executing only the authorized fallback was the right disposition. The close is nevertheless UNDER-WARRANTED as now worded and is repaired by a seam-pair disclosure cure: the seam is carried by a tier-1 bracket completion, not by the tier-2-sounding 'structural' ground the row currently offers.
rulings.grounds: Re-derived independently from the pointed bytes. (1) THE ALTERNATION THAT DEFINES THE UNIT ENDS AT MT 2:3, so the extension variant would enlarge a dialogue zone past the form its category names. Word-bound sweeps of the enumerated address vocabularies per attested spelling place the man's word for her at MT 1:15 and MT 2:2 and her word for him at MT 1:16 and MT 2:3, with the next occurrences only at MT 2:8 and MT 2:10 - so MT 2:4, MT 2:5 and MT 2:6 carry no address-vocabulary anchor and no vocative at all. The decisive surface fact, which neither packet reached: a word-final-kaf audit returns MT 1:15 = 3 gendered second-person tokens (הִנָּ֤ךְ twice and עֵינַ֥יִךְ, oshb:Song.1.15, byte tier, all 2fs) and MT 1:16 = 1 (הִנְּךָ֨, oshb:Song.1.16, byte tier, 2ms), then ZERO for every verse from MT 1:17 through MT 2:7. There is therefore no gendered second-person form anywhere in the proposed extension. The hybrid rule directs that dialogue zones be held WHOLE - a bar on atomizing them per voice-line, not a licence to extend one across material carrying none of the alternation the category is defined by. (2) THE CLOSE IS TIER-1 WARRANTED, BY BRACKET COMPLETION RATHER THAN BY VOICE-SHIFT, and the row must say so in those terms. The unit opens on a mirrored address pair - הִנָּ֤ךְ יָפָה֙ רַעְיָתִ֔י (oshb:Song.1.15, byte tier) answered by הִנְּךָ֨ יָפֶ֤ה דוֹדִי֙ (oshb:Song.1.16, byte tier) - and closes on a second mirrored address pair, כֵּ֥ן רַעְיָתִ֖י (oshb:Song.2.2, byte tier) answered by כֵּ֥ן דּוֹדִ֖י (oshb:Song.2.3, byte tier), each sitting inside the matched frame כְּשֽׁוֹשַׁנָּה֙ בֵּ֣ין הַחוֹחִ֔ים (oshb:Song.2.2, byte tier) against כְּתַפּ֨וּחַ֙ בַּעֲצֵ֣י הַיַּ֔עַר (oshb:Song.2.3, byte tier). Refrain and inclusio brackets are a tier-1 driver class standing alongside voice-shift markers, and the granularity rule provides that a unit closes on a bracket whose function is ARGUED FROM BYTES. It is argued from bytes here: the closing pair redeploys the same two enumerated address vocabularies, in the same order, as the opening pair. (3) TIER HONESTY, REQUIRED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. The two pairs are a STRUCTURAL mirror and must never be called a byte-identical inclusio: the opening frame and the closing frame share no run. Conversely the gendered contrast that identifies the two speakers in the opening pair is carried by POINTING, not by consonants - הִנָּ֤ךְ and הִנְּךָ֨ share the skeleton, word-bound sweep 3 verses book-wide - so that contrast is a BYTE-tier fact that collapses entirely at skeleton tier and may be cited at byte tier or not at all. (4) THE SEVERED RUN IS REAL, STAYS DISCLOSED, AND CANNOT BE CURED BY RE-CUTTING. Her first-person run does begin INSIDE MT 2:3 - בְּצִלּוֹ֙ חִמַּ֣דְתִּי וְיָשַׁ֔בְתִּי ... לְחִכִּֽי (oshb:Song.2.3, byte tier) - and continues into הֱבִיאַ֨נִי֙ ... וְדִגְל֥וֹ עָלַ֖י אַהֲבָֽה (oshb:Song.2.4, byte tier) with no vocative, no anchor and no gendered addressee change at the cut. But the remedy's re-cut variant is UNAVAILABLE at row granularity: spans are verse-granular, MT 2:3 must fall wholly to one side, and that verse carries the antiphon's closing anchor. The real choice is only between severing the run and dissolving the bracket, and the tier-1 bracket controls; the severed run is then carried as a disclosure, which the author has correctly installed and which must survive the re-wording ordered below. (5) CONSISTENCY WITH THIS LEDGER'S EARLIER RULINGS, checked deliberately. This applies the same principle, in the same direction, as the ruling that closed the praise frame at WEB 6:10: a byte-argued bracket may close a unit at a seam carrying no voice-shift marker. It is equally consistent with the two chapter-8 cuts that were struck, where no bracket stood at the seam and nothing else did either. The distinguishing fact throughout is the presence or absence of a byte-argued bracket AT the seam, never the presence or absence of a voice shift by itself. (6) WHAT MAY NOT CARRY THIS SEAM. The parashah inventory places SAMEKH at MT 1:14 and at MT 2:7 and NONE between, so the MT 2:7 mark does not straddle the MT 2:3|2:4 seam - it sits three verses past it - and it is tier-3, single-witness, and never directional evidence toward a later closure in either direction; the framing correction the peer made against that use is sustained and must not be re-imported. The span-relevant mark is the SAMEKH at MT 1:14 at the unit's front seam, and the row discloses it. Absence at the back seam is not counterevidence. (7) AN UNDISCLOSED CROSS-SEAM DEVICE NEITHER PACKET REACHED ON THIS ROW. The apple stem straddles this row's own back seam: כְּתַפּ֨וּחַ֙ (oshb:Song.2.3, byte tier) recurs as בַּתַּפּוּחִ֑ים (oshb:Song.2.5, byte tier), skipping MT 2:4 entirely. Object named per attested spelling and re-swept word-bound: 4 verses book-wide in four different spellings (MT 2:3, MT 2:5, MT 7:9 = web:Song.7.8, MT 8:5). A byte-true device straddling the row's own seam argues continuity against the row unless disclosed - and it IS disclosed on the forward neighbour while absent from this row, a seam-pair asymmetry, since one seam is one edit on both rows.

consequence.spec: SPANS UNCHANGED. The tiling of web:Song.1.15-Song.2.7 stays exact and is unaffected by this ruling: Song.1.15-Song.2.3 (P01-007) | Song.2.4-Song.2.6 (P01-008) | Song.2.7-Song.2.7 (P01-009). No gap, no overlap. ONE seam-pair edit at MT 2:3|2:4, installed on BOTH rows so they describe the shared seam identically. P01-007 - (a) re-word the closing-seam warrant: replace 'the closing seam is structural rather than gender-marked', which reads as a tier-2 admission, with the tier-1 BRACKET-COMPLETION driver, naming the driver class and splicing all four anchors tier-labelled (הִנָּ֤ךְ יָפָה֙ רַעְיָתִ֔י at oshb:Song.1.15 and הִנְּךָ֨ יָפֶ֤ה דוֹדִי֙ at oshb:Song.1.16; כֵּ֥ן רַעְיָתִ֖י at oshb:Song.2.2 and כֵּ֥ן דּוֹדִ֖י at oshb:Song.2.3, byte tier throughout). (b) State in the same edit that the two pairs are a STRUCTURAL mirror and NOT a byte-identical inclusio, and cite the הִנָּ֤ךְ / הִנְּךָ֨ gendered contrast at BYTE tier with the disclosure that the pair shares a skeleton (word-bound sweep: 3 verses book-wide) so the contrast does not survive at skeleton tier. (c) KEEP the cross-seam single-voice continuity disclosure the author installed - it is correct, it is the fallback the peer authorized, and it must survive the re-wording - and ADD the apple-stem straddle with the object named per attested spelling and its digit (sweep: 4 verses book-wide in four spellings; כְּתַפּ֨וּחַ֙ at oshb:Song.2.3 against בַּתַּפּוּחִ֑ים at oshb:Song.2.5, byte tier), mirroring any newly argued verse into boundary_evidence_refs. (d) KEEP the forward-neighbour refs and KEEP confidence at medium_low: it may NOT be raised on the strength of (a), because the seam remains bracket-argued rather than voice-marked and the severed run stands. (e) strongest_rejected_alternative: keep the extension rival engaged from bytes, and record that the remedy's re-cut variant is unavailable at verse granularity - one sentence plus the mandated-rival second sentence, no third. (f) Do NOT install, and strike if introduced: any appeal to the MT 2:7 mark as directional evidence toward a later close. (g) UNCHANGED and not to be re-opened: MT 2:1 stays HELD as gender-unmarked (אֲנִי֙ חֲבַצֶּ֣לֶת, oshb:Song.2.1, byte tier); the 1cp splices עַרְשֵׂ֖נוּ (oshb:Song.1.16) and בָּתֵּ֨ינוּ֙ (oshb:Song.1.17) stay; the MT 1:17 ketiv/qere disclosure stays as installed, qere רַהִיטֵ֖נוּ (oshb:Song.1.17, byte tier), that verse being one of only 4 K/Q-bearing verses book-wide, single-witness. unit_type stays dialogue_exchange. P01-008 - CONSEQUENCE ROW, seam-pair partner, must be touched. (h) Install the SAME bracket-completion wording at its FRONT seam so both rows describe the shared seam in the same terms and neither states a warrant the other contradicts. (i) Its apple-stem disclosure is VERIFIED CORRECT as written (word-bound, 4 verses, four attested spellings, MT 7:9 correctly dual-cited) - do not re-cut it, and mirror that same object and digit onto P01-007 rather than authoring a second differently-worded version of it. (j) PRECISION REPAIR, run as part of the embrace-colon sweep already ordered elsewhere for this same pair rather than as a spot fix: MT 2:6 reads לְרֹאשִׁ֔י (oshb:Song.2.6, byte tier) against רֹאשִׁ֔י (oshb:Song.8.3, byte tier), the lamed present in the earlier verse and absent in the later, so the colon is NOT identical across the two verses at skeleton tier either; state the recurrence for the sub-runs that do match and name the lamed difference. (k) Do NOT re-open its own 2:6|2:7 boundary, which rests on the attested oath anchor הִשְׁבַּ֨עְתִּי אֶתְכֶ֜ם בְּנ֤וֹת יְרוּשָׁלִַ֨ם֙ (oshb:Song.2.7, byte tier) and is not in issue. NOT consequence rows, stated so they are not edited speculatively: P01-006 (its back seam 1:14|1:15 is untouched) and P01-009 (its front seam 2:6|2:7 is untouched). No chunk ordinals change, since no row is added or dissolved. TESTS each cure must pass - the test that killed the original: (i) delete every sentence naming a parashah mark and BOTH seams must still stand on spliced, tier-labelled bytes; (ii) the closing-seam warrant must name a tier-1 DRIVER CLASS and quote the bytes that carry it - the word 'structural' standing alone fails, and any wording implying a voice shift AT the cut is byte-false and fails; (iii) no recurrence sentence may assert a byte-identity or a skeleton-identity that collate does not return, which the two mirrored pairs and the embrace colon each fail if overstated; (iv) every device straddling the shared seam is disclosed on BOTH rows, in the same object wording and with the same digit.
